the risk factors associated with changes in antibody levels during the peri-wean period were multifactorial and included the breed and the plane of nutrition of the calf, as well as its clinical condition at weaning.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the risk of exposure to a BRD pathogen during the peri-weanning period may be influenced by the breed of calf, the level of exposure to the pathogen during the pre-weanning period, the calf’s ability to respond to the pathogen and the calf’s health status during the peri-weening period.
calves with a high respiratory score, high BVDV S/N at d −14 and a haptoglobin level of between 1 and 1.6 at d − 14 are more susceptible to BRD.
the risk factors associated with the serological responses to the various BRD pathogens during peri-weaning are complex, multifactorial and not well understood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pre-weaning antibody status of calves may be used as a tool to identify calves at risk of BRD.
the peri-weaning time period may be a key period in terms of the risk of exposure to BRD in dairy calves.
we should be more careful about the use of seroconversion as a measure of exposure to a pathogen.
